tools.reason: Calibrated option-picker (Jev + permutation averaging). Used as the task->model-tier router. Ran live here: routed a trivial README edit to haiku at 1.0 confidence. A classifier call is far cheaper than asking a frontier model to reason about its own tier.

tools.popularity_claim: 19 stars / 3 commits as rendered on the repo page — thin and young. Adopted on WORKING EVIDENCE, not popularity; pinned, and the router degrades to a static table if it breaks.

tools.reason: Already installed in this harness as anthropic-skills:skill-creator. With ~150 skills the real failure mode is description collision and mis-triggering; this is the only candidate that MEASURES trigger accuracy. Better triggering is a direct token saving.

tools.reason: pip-installable here, but our MCP toolkit needs no framework: a stdlib JSON-RPC server has zero supply-chain surface, no install step in CI, and starts instantly. We took the typed-tool-decorator shape without the dependency.
tools.pattern_taken: Typed tool declarations with JSON Schema per tool -> tools/mcp/gm_toolkit.py

tools.reason: Config-as-JSON conditional routing is the right shape, but it is a proxy server for multi-provider API traffic. We do not make raw provider calls from the game repo — Claude Code is the client. Running a gateway would add a process to route traffic that does not flow through us.
tools.pattern_taken: Declarative routes.json with conditions + explicit fallback -> tools/farm/routes.json

tools.reason: Dispatcher/subagent-delegation patterns are sound, but adding ~50 opinionated workflow skills on top of our ~150 multiplies trigger collisions and RAISES token burn — the opposite of the goal.
tools.pattern_taken: Compressed-handback subagent delegation (strict word budget + fixed output format) -> used for this very evaluation

tools.reason: Path-addressed context store is the closest match to our farm/routing/state goals, but AGPL plus an external service is disproportionate for a ~120-file static-hosted game.
tools.pattern_taken: Path-addressed, gated context loading -> extends existing .claude/context-manifests/

tools.reason: Its 61 detectors are DOM/CSS-based and cannot see a Godot canvas. The valuable part is the shape, not the rules.
tools.pattern_taken: Deterministic script pre-filters; the model only reads findings. Already how security-sentinel.sh works — now the stated standard for all new gates.

tools.reason: Index-and-query-instead-of-read targets our exact token problem, but its token-reduction figures are self-reported, it is young, and AGPL + a local vector DB is heavy for ~120 files that ripgrep searches instantly.
tools.pattern_taken: Query, do not read whole files — enforced by context-manifests and the grep-first rule
